Carrot, as sold from Moldova Noua (mining area M) (mining-affected area) had lead higher at 120 µg/kg, against 60 µg/kg for Borlova (reference area) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iosif Gergen, Monica Harmanescu · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Application of principal component analysis in the pollution assessment with heavy metals of vegetable food chain in the old mining areas</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal6:156</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>

<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as carrot

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers carrot in 5 forms kept separate in every comparison: carrot, as sold (1,206 results), carrot, powder or ground (60 results), carrot, cooked (11 results), carrot, peeled or flesh (8 <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-carrot" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-carrot-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of carrot, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach carrot

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach carrot comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Carrot, as sold from Ruschita old mining area (R) (mining-affected area) had lead higher at 2,110 µg/kg, against 30 µg/kg for Borlova reference area (Ref) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/harmanescu2011-banat-mining-vegetables-metals|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Harmanescu M, Alda LM, Bordean DM, Gogoasa I, Gergen I · 2011</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/harmanescu2011-banat-mining-vegetables-metals">Heavy metals health risk assessment for population via consumption of vegetables grown in old mining area; a case study: Banat County, Romania</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal 2011, 5:64</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/harmanescu2011-banat-mining-vegetables-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, carrot, as sold from Wastewater irrigation (WW) (experiment) had Co higher at 288 µg/kg, against 7 µg/kg for Control (freshwater irrigation) (Control (Fw)) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/el-batal2023-carrot-wastewater-selenium-nanoparticles|23]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">El-Batal AI, El-Sayyad GS, El-Ghamry A, Abdel-Megeed A · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/el-batal2023-carrot-wastewater-selenium-nanoparticles">Effect of selenium nanoparticles on heavy metal accumulation in carrot (Daucus carota) irrigated with wastewater</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Biologia</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/el-batal2023-carrot-wastewater-selenium-nanoparticles">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A third study found that carrot, as sold from Ruschita (mining area R) (mining-affected area) had lead higher at 2,110 µg/kg, against 60 µg/kg for Borlova (reference area) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iosif Gergen, Monica Harmanescu · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Application of principal component analysis in the pollution assessment with heavy metals of vegetable food chain in the old mining areas</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal6:156</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-carrot" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-carrot" data-question="How do heavy metals get into carrot?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into carrot?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, carrot from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than carrot from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iosif Gergen, Monica Harmanescu · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Application of principal component analysis in the pollution assessment with heavy metals of vegetable food chain in the old mining areas</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal6:156</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Carrot, as sold from Moldova Noua (mining area M) (mining-affected area) had lead higher at 120 µg/kg, against 60 µg/kg for Borlova (reference area) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iosif Gergen, Monica Harmanescu · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Application of principal component analysis in the pollution assessment with heavy metals of vegetable food chain in the old mining areas</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal6:156</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-carrot" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-carrot" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in carrot?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in carrot?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, carrot, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (3.65 µg/kg) and the highest in SEARO (60 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in WPRO (9.54 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (300 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in carrot is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 8 results from 4 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/laizu2007-dhaka-vegetables-arsenic-speciation|34]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Laizu J · 2007</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/laizu2007-dhaka-vegetables-arsenic-speciation">Speciation of arsenic in vegetables and their correlation with inorganic phosphate level</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bangladesh Journal of Pharmacology 2007;
